pr_body:
Fixes #14343. Adds the missing implementation of EVP_PKEY_supports_digest_nid for provider-based (non-legacy) keys. The ASN1_PKEY_CTRL_SUPPORTS_MD_NID was not handled for non-legacy.

The code uses EVP_PKEY_get_params to "assert" a value, i.e. it sets a value of input OSSL_PARAM and expect the get_params function to fail if the assertion is invalid.
pr_comments:
This function is pretty much a hack that should be taken care of in a different manner.  I know that @mattcaswell has some ideas about capabilities, while I would like to remove the need for the whole NID split-and-join-again by making it possible to offer sigalg implementations (i.e. making it possible to fetch EVP_SIGNATUREs like "SHA1WithRSAencryption").

Either way, I don't think it's wise to push this particular functionality on providers.
At.  All.

issue_context.title: EVP_PKEY_supports_digest_nid does not work with provider-side keys
issue_context.body:
I am facing a regression of #7348. During TLS negotiation is the TPM provider asked to sign using an unsupported hash, provided by the default provider. The TPM cannot sign using external hash algorithms, so despite a hash algorithm is implemented by some other provider it cannot be used for digest-signing using TPM-based keys.

To solve this in a generic way, the `EVP_PKEY_supports_digest_nid` has been created some years ago and used in [`ssl/t1_lib.c:check_cert_usable`](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/master/ssl/t1_lib.c#L3045) to check whether a particular hash is compatible with a particular sigalg. It is however based on `evp_pkey_asn1_ctrl`, which works for legacy keys only, so the old problem re-appears after migration to providers.

I found few possibilities how this could be solved "in the provider world", but none of them is perfect. The trouble is there seems to be no mechanism to "check" something.
 * The `EVP_PKEY_CTX_set_signature_md` could be (mis)used to check compatibility of a hash, but this requires creation of a temporary PKEY_CTX and initialization of a sign/verify operation (e.g. `EVP_PKEY_sign_init`). These steps can be seen as a waste of computing resources, decreasing the performance as it needs to be called for each candidate sigalg.
 * There could be a new KEYMGMT settable parameter such as `OSSL_PKEY_PARAM_MD_SUPPORTED` that will only test validity of the argument, instead of setting it. But this is also a slight misuse of the API.
 * Or there could be a completely new KEYMGMT function to check various assertions (`OSSL_FUNC_KEYMGMT_ASSERT_PARAMS`) that would consume e.g. the `OSSL_PKEY_PARAM_MD_SUPPORTED`, verify the assertion ("this MD is supported") and return 0/1 accordingly. It seems to me that e.g. `ASN1_PKEY_CTRL_CMS_IS_RI_TYPE_SUPPORTED` might be also unsupported by providers, so this might be usable also for others.

The `OSSL_FUNC_KEYMGMT_ASSERT_PARAMS` function feels to be the cleanest solution, but is it acceptable to introduce yet another KEYMGMT function? (It's not very invasive and it's quite generic hence reusable.) Or do you see other options how the `EVP_PKEY_supports_digest_nid` can be implemented for non-legacy?
comments:
> * There could be a new KEYMGMT settable parameter such as `OSSL_PKEY_PARAM_MD_SUPPORTED` that will only test validity of the argument, instead of setting it. But this is also a slight misuse of the API.

Wouldn't that be better implemented as a *gettable* parameter?

I have another fairly radical idea; make sigalgs directly fetchable.  I cannot see why libcrypto needs to go through the business of splitting a sigalg into hash and pkey algos, just to join them backtogether to perform the signing operation.  The benefit with that is that libcrypto would have no need at all to keep that internal cross reference table saying what goes together.
It will possibly work for GOST, but I'm not sure that it work for RSA that allows many hash algorithms to be used.

Having a gettable parameter is also a possibility. But since a TPM usually supports multiple digest algorithms, there would be multiple parameters of the same type (if that is allowed) or some array structure (which is cumbersome to use). A muti-value gettable parameter sounds nice though.

Having fetchable sigalgs sounds nice too. It might also simplify the EVP_DigestSign API and bring some automation to the "algorithm-id" business.

Er, @beldmit, can you tell me why fetching "sha1WithRSAEncryption" and getting an EVP_SIGNATURE wouldn't be workable?

> Having fetchable sigalgs sounds nice too. It might also simplify the EVP_DigestSign API and bring some automation to the "algorithm-id" business.

Yes, exactly.
(although, I would prefer not to overload the EVP_DigestSign API, it's already confusing enough as it is)
Yes, it will be workable. My fault.

Come to think of it, this isn't even a novel idea...  this thought exists in pre-3.0, but is implemented in terms of EVP_MD:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/a88ea7dfdfba2c34bd575076f12f06d80dd2c0c2/crypto/evp/m_sha1.c#L280-L292

Now that we have an `EVP_SIGNATURE`, that would seem like the perfect method for that sort of thing
If I remember correctly, there were some tricks when there was more than one compatible algorithm...

I think this boils down to us needing a way for a provider to say that this signature algorithm can only be used with digests from itself (or more generally, that if any one operations comes from a provider, all must do so).  For most providers and quite a number of HSMs, it isn't necessary to fetch the digest from the same device as the signature -- we definitely don't want to lose this capability.

Having yet another look at this, I'm not sure I understand what's happening.  If the key is a provider key, then `evp_pkey_asn1_ctrl()` should return -2, no?  In that case, the fallback code should kick in, no?  As far as I know, that code *does* support provider side keys.

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/8287a4c3b2230f8df109f5eb34171fa0058add2c/crypto/evp/p_lib.c#L1254-L1265

My point was that legacy engines have `ASN1_PKEY_CTRL_DEFAULT_MD_NID` **and** `ASN1_PKEY_CTRL_SUPPORTS_MD_NID`, each behaving differently. However, for providers there is only `EVP_PKEY_get_default_digest_nid` because the `EVP_PKEY_supports_digest_nid` falls back to (behaves exactly as) `EVP_PKEY_get_default_digest_nid`.
`ASN1_PKEY_CTRL_SUPPORTS_MD_NID` is new in master / 3.0, so no production engine should support it.  We *could* very simply revert ecbb2fca9301ef22b15beb30c4c0303b29846935

My reasoning is that it's a bit misplaced to ask the key type implementation what digests are supported, since that's really about the signature implementation.  However, that's how the legacy implementations work, and as long as libssl hasn't been refactored to handle signature algorithms that libcrypto doesn't have internal knowledge of, the legacy code should keep on working with very little change.

Yeah, it doesn't fit the provider mechanisms. The ecbb2fc was introduced as an option for a TPM (and similar engines) to indicate what sigalgs can be used. It would be sad to revert that commit without having an alternate solution. Offering only one (default) digest during TLS negotiation will cause unnecessary handshake failures.

> The ecbb2fc was introduced as an option for a TPM (and similar engines) to indicate what sigalgs can be used...

... gotcha, and I've recently argued that this should really be done by fetching them directly instead of doing the split-and-join dance with the sigalg identity, see #14467.

Note that with fetchable sigalgs, it would mean that they're fetched very early, and of `check_cert_usable()` would have to check support of the sigalg id (be it a NID or a name in string form) against that, or be fetched on demand, which would essentially make `check_cert_usable()` irrelevant, as the usability comes down to the fetch result.

In a similar vein, we could simply keep doing the split dance, but then simply call `EVP_DigestSIgnInit_ex()` or `EVP_DigestVerifyInit_ex()` (whichever applies) and use the result to verify that the sigalg is acceptable.  I'd find that kind of solution much more feasible, and most of all future proof, than making `EVP_PKEY_supports_digest_nid()` work with providers.
With #14467 the ecbb2fc can be reverted. (I was not aware of that, sorry.) Only I wish it could be in 3.0.0 as it impacts usability of TLS with TPM-based keys.
Unfortunately, it might take a longer while than I expected to get #14467 in.  In the mean time, a cheap solution would be what I proposed, to do a check using `EVP_DigestSignInit_ex()`

review_comments: You've added a new parameter but it isn't used by anything on the provider side.  I.e. this does exactly nothing.

It is supposed to be used by external providers (only). It's the same as `ASN1_PKEY_CTRL_SUPPORTS_MD_NID`. That parameter is also not used by any of the internal openssl providers. It's there for the external providers who impose additional restrictions on digests that could be used with their keys, such as the TPM2.
If an external provider supports it, our internal ones must do also.
Getting a parameter overwrites it's contents, in this case the short name.  I don't think this is desirable.

The output OSSL_PARAMs are irrelevant. The code tests whether a given short name is in the list of supported digests, so only the int result of EVP_PKEY_get_params is used.

I agree this is weird, but with only GET and SET operations there is no easy way to determine if a certain value (the short name) is in a certain list on the provider side (the list of supported digests). This is what the CTRL operation was doing for the legacy and there seems to be no equivalent.

An alternate solution would be to retrieve all supported digests and check whether the one is in the list. This list may include various synonyms (SHA256, SHA-256, SHA2-256) so it will not be short. But I can do it that way, if you agree that would be better. It's probably a cleaner solution than misusing GET for doing an assertion.

BTW, what would be your preferred way to obtain a list? A set of OSSL_PARAMs with identical names, or e.g. a semicolon separated list such as `"SHA256:SHA-256:SHA2-256"`.

BTW2, it is not possible to simply fetch all digest algorithms provided by the PKEY's provider because the individual PKEY may be restricted only for usage with a specific digest. The list of supported digests is a property of a PKEY, not the provider itself.
However, we are very strict about "get" parameters being received and "set" parameters being sent.  This is doing both with a "get" parameter.  This is **wrong**.
This works but there are other ways of detecting if something was modified.  Look at `OSSL_PARAM_modified()`.
